Heat treatment above the β-transus temperature (HIP 950) significantly coarsened the microstructure giving elongated blocky α grains along with some equiaxed α grains and the average α grain thickness increased to around 33.5 µm (Figure 6.4c & 6.5c and Table 6.2).
Finally, the wrought CP-Ti had a recrystallized, equiaxed grain structure (Figure 6.4d and Figure 6.5d,e) and the average grain size was measured on two orthogonal planes.
For the plane with the TD direction oriented normal to the plane (Figure 6.5e), the grain size was around 32.5 µm (Table 6.2).

After the HIP 730 treatment (below β transus), the α grain size became 44% thicker than for the ASB condition and the equiaxed grains increased in number; however, much of the acicular structure of the ASB samples remained.
In contrast, heat treatment above the β-transus (HIP 950) and slow furnace cooling completely destroyed the acicular structure resulting in large blocky grains along with some equiaxed grains.

In this regard, the coarser initial β grain size of the X-HIP 950 samples will lead to a coarser retained β phase that puts less constraint on the coarsening the α grain structure compared to the Z-HIP 950 samples.
Additionally, HIP coarsened the grain size with increasing temperature (Figure 6.5) and decreasing strength with microstructure coarsening is commonly observed for CP-Ti alloys [9, 360-362].
